notes.title: Devlog #19 - VFX Update!
notes.notes:
Howdy partners!

Today we want to showcase our brand new VFX! We decided to finally update them, and honestly, we love them. Right now we mostly have animal-related ones, but there is also a cactus and smoke of absolute deception. Enjoy!

1. Animal reactions

They show up when animals react to their surroundings and states, like sleeping, eating or being herded. The icons were hand-drawn on a cardboard-like texture and animated in Unreal Engine’s particle system, Niagara. We wanted to make them look as if the Cowboy himself scribbled them carelessly, without any fancy tools (let alone skills). We love the new update – they give out a cozy, homely vibe!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/2c437219283d923a4f656a7e095cbd2752ba4caf.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/b0302b52a94dda9280ecb3e90824bcbb1c9d1fdf.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/a230b7b600c276539709d4d827ecdb58882ffec6.gif[/img]

2. Smokescreen of Deception

Some of the inner workings of our game aren't exactly, uh, visually appealing. To combat this, we use a little trick called Smokescreen (it is not called that, we made it up). We use it in many different places. Here you can see the quest with Ruff Raymond, where the shooting range appears. Poof!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/a230b7b600c276539709d4d827ecdb58882ffec6.gif[/img]

3. Cactus juice

The cacti no longer bleed when being cut down! (Yeah, they used to do that. But now we un-placeholdered that!) It now has this beautiful, green juice splashing out of it. Not cardboard-like this time, we aimed for a little bit more realistic look with this one. They look way better now. Made using simple hand-drawn textures and some Niagara magic!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/498302bed4e6f32aa8516a1e51b95be39a1f715a.gif[/img]
 
4. The “Howdy Exclamation Point”

We also recently coded this feature where if an NPC has something you could talk to them about, an exclamation point appears over their head. For some time we had a simple placeholder icon there, but look a this new one – also hand-drawn, and also in that cute style that the animals and smoke have!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ae19051f45117432b38e7aad419d2e47dea03b5d.gif[/img]

So what do you think? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message at our X (well, Twitter...) – [url=https://x.com/OddQubit]@OddQubit[/url]. We’d also love to have you over on our growing Discord server – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/vK7ee3eb]link[/url]]. Happy trails, friend.

notes.title: DEVLOG #17 – OPTIMIZATION
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]

Every game starts rough. At first, we’re focused on gameplay and visuals, not performance. It’s all prototypes, heavy assets, wild ideas… and suddenly, it’s running at 15 FPS. Yep, we’ve been there too. But now we’re on a mission to hit 60.

We optimize two big areas: [b]CPU[/b], meaning game logic, collisions, movement, AI, and [b]GPU[/b], so everything visual.

Optimization means finding [b]smarter ways[/b] to do things and cutting what’s too heavy.


[h3]Farewell, Nanite[/h3]

Early on, we were thrilled about Nanite, Unreal Engine 5’s [b]fancy rendering tech[/b] that lets you use [b]ultra-detailed models[/b]. But as our world filled up, problems piled on: stutters, memory spikes, performance dips... We ran a ton of tests and eventually accepted the truth: Nanite just [b]wasn’t the right fit[/b] for our game.

[b]So we cut it[/b]. Maybe we’ll get back to it in our next game? It worked wonders in Expedition 33, but our guess is that projects really need a Nanite-oriented approach from the get-go.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/4df564506913f697194177563782d3898a2fcb42.gif[/img]

[i]Nanite triangle visualisation of the main street in our town, Bravestand.
Anything black is not nanite – the colorful ones are. You can see how the triangles change when you get closer.[/i]


💡further reading: "[url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine]What is Nanite?[/url]"



[h3]Draw Calls, LODs, and Distant Tree Drama[/h3]

In an open world, managing [b]draw calls[/b] is crucial. Each one is a [b]command[/b] to the GPU to render something. We fight the flood with [b]mesh instancing[/b], meaning 100 identical trees are grouped together under a single draw call, and [b]HLODs[/b] (Hierarchical Level of Detail), which [b]simplify [/b]faraway stuff into [b]chunky geometry[/b].

We also rely heavily on [b]LODs[/b] — [b]simpler versions of objects[/b] used at a distance. Auto-generated ones usually work, but Unreal struggles with things like trees, often dropping entire branches. Our artist is currently handcrafting tree LODs to fix that.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/02ed9d7fcdb5191b75bc8ce6c139e943ba2bb46c.gif[/img]

[i]Visualisation of the changing LODs of the train tracks and nature around them.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/6751cb05c06013697c40c948799a1be59a37b34a.png[/img]

[i]Visualisation of the density of the triangles in certain spots.[/i]


💡further reading: "[url=https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/r2n/unreal-engine-polycount-optimization-and-draw-calls]Polycount, Optimization and Draw Calls[/url]"



[h3]Lighting on a Leash[/h3]


We use fully [b]dynamic lighting[/b], which looks great but [b]hits performance hard[/b]. Most games bake lighting (pre-render it), but we wanted a real-time sun, beautiful mornings, and picturesque sunsets.

To keep it manageable, we [b]reduced light precision[/b] and added a graphics setting so players can choose how often the sun moves to best suit the might of their machines.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/82008d202f8299307fe533f331ce2948a4784e57.png[/img]

[i]Visualisation of lighting of a scene, in this case the town of Bravestand from a different angle.
The orange blobs signify overlaps of light coming from different light sources, which is more costly performance-wise.
[/i]


💡further reading: "[url=https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lighting-the-environment?application_version=4.27]Lighting the Environment[/url]"



[h3]CPU: Simpler Collisions, Smarter Code[/h3]


First target? [b]Collisions[/b]. And by collisions, we don’t mean just bumping into stuff – this concept includes [b]overlaps [/b]and big [b]trigger volumes[/b]: checking if animals are in their homes and if NPCs are at a certain location.

We [b]simplified them[/b] to [b]spheres[/b], [b]capsules[/b], and [b]boxes[/b] – as little complex shapes as possible. Most moving objects either have [b]no real collision[/b], or we fake it. Why? Because checking for hits and overlaps constantly drains CPU. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/208665fc6f2d6b21db5923723e5fa681497ad844.gif[/img]

[i]Visualisation of the collisions of different objects at the Saloon in town.
The bottles, for example, have spherical collisions.[/i]


💡further reading: "[url=https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/8d8P/unreal-engine-fortnite-how-to-optimize-collision-performance]How to Optimize Collision Performance[/url]"



[h3]Data Loads and Animal AI[/h3]


Our world runs on [b]big databases[/b] for animals, plants, and buildings. And in the case of buildings, every single module is a separate entry, and some buildings have dozens of modules! Pulling data was [b]slow[/b], but our backend dev sprinkled some magic and sped things up — though it’s still a work in progress.

We’re also refining [b]NPCs [/b]and [b]animals[/b], which are [b]complex [/b]due to animation, AI, collisions, and skeletal meshes. For example, animals and characters have 5fps animations when you’re not looking. ;)

We keep tweaking their behavior logic to make them [b]smarter [/b]and [b]leaner[/b].
To track what’s slowing us down, we use the [b]Unreal Insights tool[/b].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/8adfbda26368cfc2225c851c967fdbf994def63c.png[/img]

[i]Our main investigation tool for diving deep into optimization issues – the Unreal Insights graph.[/i]

notes.title: DEVLOG #16 – GAME LOOP
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]

Cowboy Life is a game where time matters. Days and weeks pass, and each morning brings a new mix of farming chores, crafting, exploring, and wild west trouble.


[h3]Daily Routine[/h3]

Most days start [b]on your farm[/b]. You’ll water crops, feed animals, and do all the work needed to keep things growing. It’s not just for fun, you and your animals need food!

But farming isn’t only for survival. The townsfolk will send [b]requests[/b] and [b]orders[/b], and to fulfill them, you’ll need to produce more [b]advanced items[/b]. That means [b]upgrading your farm[/b], building new workstations, and gathering resources like wood, clay, and stone. Later on, you’ll explore mines to collect metal ores, too.

Crafting takes time at first, but later on (in the full version of the game) you will be able to [b]hire workers[/b] to help out. So don’t just stand around waiting – use that time to handle other tasks. There's always something to do on the farm!

The requests come through the [b]mailbox[/b], so [b]check your mail[/b] every morning!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/16bca688f5a322b014d1e7ca27500bacf6d75fb5.png[/img]


[h3]Neighbors & Quests[/h3]

The nearby town, [b]Bravestand[/b], is full of u[b]nique characters[/b] – each with their own story, habits, and problems. Some want help. Some want change. All of them are [b]part of a bigger mystery[/b] involving [b]drought[/b], bandits, and something strange going on in the hills:

you’ll take on [b]quests[/b], investigate, [b]duel[/b], deliver goods, search for legendary items, and uncover secrets. 


Talking to people and [b]learning their routines[/b] will help a lot – some NPCs only appear in certain places at certain times.

They will go about their days with or without your help and even [b]initiate meetings[/b] on their own. Missed one? You’ll have to track them down and reschedule.

And we have even more NPC-related mechanics planned for the future, such as [b]gifting [/b] and [b]relationship-building[/b]!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/87ffbaec623f07c178e1d438db26f6ac52443d79.png[/img]


[h3]The World [/h3]

[b]Exploration[/b] is important too. While waiting for the craft to finish or an NPC to return from whatever trip they embarked upon, you can [b]head out into the world[/b].

The map isn’t huge, but it’s [b]open[/b], and packed with beautiful, distinct [b]locations[/b], [b]secrets[/b], and [b]treasure chests[/b]. Some may be locked, and the keys are often tied to story progress, so exploration and quests go hand in hand!

Just be careful – some areas are [b]full of bandits[/b]. Bring a weapon, and if possible, upgrade it. Weapon upgrades cost money, so maybe it’s time to fulfil another job... But wait! You’ll need bricks for that, which means upgrading your stone workshop... which means chopping wood... [i]which means…[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/3b6460b4989509fc0cbc388730961b4324bacec7.png[/img]


[h3]Back to the Axe[/h3]

In the end, it always circles [b]back to the basics[/b]:

- gathering
- crafting
- building
- surviving


[h3]That’s the loop! [/h3]
And here’s always so much more waiting to be discovered.

See you out there, cowboy. Yeah, and don’t forget to check that mailbox.



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]].


Happy trails, friend.

notes.title: DEVLOG #15 – CHARACTERS
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]

Hello, friends! Thank you so much for appreciating our last devlog on reworked progression! Today’s topic is… [b]characters[/b]!

What makes a game like Stardew Valley so cozy and familiar? [b]The characters![/b] The ones we trade with, the ones we get to know and explore their world. It’s a big deal for us while working on “Cowboy Life”, making our characters [b]likeable[/b] and [b]memorable[/b].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5a44babb4b2e88cc1b46d623cca0bf3480913c31.png[/img]



[h3]1. Shaping a concept[/h3]


Before adding any character, we define their [b]traits [/b]and [b]motivations [/b]and link them with others and the protagonist meaningfully.

Instead of simple stereotypes, our characters have [b]conflicting traits[/b], and hidden secrets that [b]the player can uncover[/b].

Some of them will go through a lot, trying to find [b]their own role in the world[/b], learning and proving themselves worthy, but will emerge stronger and happier [b]because of players' actions.[/b]

Like in classic Disney’s films, our characters have [b]meaningful names[/b]: some of them reflect the character’s personality, others – their occupation or behavior. Some names even reference real-life historical figures, likeour town architect, Frank Lloyd.



[h3]2. How our NPCs affect (and are affected by) gameplay[/h3]


[b]– Engaging NPC routines[/b]

Your neighbors like to have a drink or a round of cards at the Saloon in the evening, they go to church on Sundays, or visit their favorite spots in the wilderness in their free time… [b]Just like real people do![/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e0206525883aeb8cc861936c82b003487193ffe5.png[/img]


[b]– Part of the bigger picture[/b]

In small communities, [b]word spreads fast.[/b]

If you complete a quest for one character, their best friend will know about it,
and if you do something that benefits everyone, all characters [b]will be grateful[/b] (some discounts maybe?).


[b]– Bringing the Wild West to life [/b]

They do more than give you quests. They let you discover hidden secrets, surprises, and personal adventures. One moment, a friendly chat might start an exciting quest. Next, a mysterious stranger might refuse to help until you prove yourself worthy of trust.

[b]Each meeting[/b] shows you [b]a new layer[/b], leading you deeper into your cowboy adventure.



[h3]3. Writing realistic dialogue[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/87ffbaec623f07c178e1d438db26f6ac52443d79.png[/img]


“Cowboy Life” does of course take place in the Wild West. We all know our howdies and yeehaws, but we cannot allow dialogue to become [b]a caricature[/b]. Keepin’ it stylized, but [b]moderate[/b], partner.

Characters’ personalities [b]affect the way they speak[/b]. A well-educated pharmacist will have a [b]different way of expressing[/b] herself than a simpleton living out in the mountains.

The story is an important driver, but since it's not an RPG, but a mix of RPG and a simulator, and plenty of people will want to click through dialogues. And that's alright! That’s why we take extra time to make the dialogues as short and saturated as possible.

All our dialogue is [b]written [/b]and [b]programmed [/b]using a narrative design tool called Articy:Draft.



[h3]4. Implementation[/h3]

Every character needs a [b]3D model[/b], of course. Before that usually comes a concept sketch,
but as we are quite a small studio, we do not have a [b]Concept Artist[/b].

Instead, [b]visual references[/b] are gathered, usually by the [b]Narrative Designer[/b], and delivered to
our 3D Artist with a short description of the character’s vibe. Often these references are
even pictures of real-life people: actors, historic figures, or people we, the devs, actually know!

For example, references for our charismatic and broad-shouldered carpenter, Ted, were taken from our designer’s [b]husband[/b]. For our Mayor – of that [b]husband's grandfather[/b], a military physicist specializing in explosives. One of the [b]most notorious bandits[/b] in our game is modeled after a… well, we will keep this one a secret a little longer.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/02ccdcdebb4448975d74f73524fd5501c26da0ca.png[/img]


Then, it’s just designing the callendar, giving the character stuff to sell, setting up their homes, their shops, and their routines. 



[h3]The community[/h3]

And how does the player character fit in all this?

The community of [b]Bravestand [/b]is troubled by [b]bandits[/b], [b]drought [/b]and [b]distrust[/b]. Not very cozy, right? It’s the player’s role to make the townfolk find trust again, to stand together against the inequities of the selfish and the tyranny of evil men, to [b]live up to the name[/b] of their little town!

It’s you, the player, that is the agent of hope, finding [b]inner peace through helping others. [/b]

We hope you’ll find it satisfying and rewarding!


[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]].


Happy trails, friend.

notes.title: DEVLOG #14 – PROGRESSION SYSTEM: REWORKED!
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]


Hello, friends! Big news: [b]new progression system![/b] 🎉

We’ve got super exciting news to share with you! We’ve been working very hard these past few months, and we’re quite proud of the result. And what is that? [b]Completely reworked progression[/b]! Not to brag, but “Cowboy” [b]feels like a whole new game now[/b]…



[b]What was progression like before?[/b]

Honestly… it wasn’t great. You could only [b]unlock things by progressing the narrative[/b]. For example, you couldn’t build or craft anything unless you finished a specific quest.

And, more importantly from our perspective, managing the progression was incredibly hard. The simplest change, like wanting a certain craft to be available even a bit earlier would require tinkering with the quests and narrative, and those are a very delicate web, especially in a non-linear game like ours!



[b]What’s it like now?[/b]

So, we decided to [b]add a completely new layer[/b]: good old fashioned [b]experience points[/b], so you can level up! And not just one set for those, though. We added [b]three experience pillars[/b]: Farm, Fame, and Frontier!


– [b]Farm Points[/b]: Earned by upgrading your farm.

– [b]Fame Points[/b]: Earned by helping and interacting with NPCs, and doing quests.

– [b]Frontier Points[/b]: Earned by exploring and making new, more advanced things.


You can see your points and levels in the [b]“Progression” menu[/b]. It also shows what cool stuff you’ll unlock at each level. [b]Need points fast[/b]? Complete fun challenges under each pillar to get more!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/c08c4eb8177f98f39fddab4774c5aeba4a15ba6e.jpg[/img]

Here’s a sneak peek into our work-in-progress of the progression screen. Do not get too attached to it just yet, we are working on overhauling the UI too!



[b]What can you unlock?[/b]

There’s a lot of freedom when it comes to that. Depending on which progression tree you want to go with, rewards may vary. They include:

– new buildings
– item crafts
– forage possibilities
– entire game features
– special dialogue lines

... and many others!

And, these new dialogue lines aren’t just for chatting – they [b]start quests[/b], and even [b]whole storylines[/b].



[b]How does it work?[/b]

Say you’re talking to an NPC, and you see[b] a greyed-out dialogue line[/b]. It says you [b]need Farm Level 3[/b] to select it. You check your “Progression” menu – you’re at Farm Level 2 and need more points ... 

... What can you do about it?

– complete a farming quest on your farm (like sowing fields)
– complete some challenges: there's lots and lots of those, so there’s always something to do!

Boom, now you’re [b]Farm Level 3[/b] – go back to the NPC and unlock an awesome quest!



[b]Was that an easy rework?[/b]

Well, it wasn’t – the new system [b]has to work with all the other systems[/b], and itself be easy enough to manage and maintain. Also, now we can’t simply say “you can’t build that before that quest is completed”. You can [b]gain experience through many different activities[/b], so the [b]math has to be perfect[/b] if we want the game to be balanced.

[b]So far though, it’s looking good![/b] Now, if we want to give the player some craft earlier on in the game, we just change its availability level from 10 to 7. Done!

All in all, we think that “Cowboy Life” is now way more engaging because there’s always something to do. On the other hand, if you don’t want to do quests, and meetings, but simply explore, farm, and make a mark on the land, you should also get some experience, and level up.


[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]].


Happy trails, friend.

notes.title: DEVLOG #13 – NEW PLAYTESTS AND PROGRESS
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]


Hello, friends!

Thanks for liking our updates! We’re so happy that we want to share more with you – [b]more playtests are coming soon[/b]! No exact date yet, but make sure to click [b]"Request Access"[/b] so you don’t miss it!

[b]Why more playtests[/b], though? Since receiving feedback after the last one, we’ve been working hard to make the game better for you! This time, we’ve focused on improving the gameplay, especially that related to the [b]NPCs[/b] and the [b]animals[/b], and making the game [b]easier to understand[/b], an get into the flow of. We want to know what you think!



[h2]Here’s what’s new:[/h2]

[b]– more NPCs and life on the level[/b]

All characters now have [b]routines[/b]! You can talk to them and [b]learn their schedules[/b], and check this info [b]on the map[/b] or in your journal. But, just like in real life [i](hey, it's a life sim after all)[/i] some characters are hard to catch because they move around a lot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ccd0998817611e93d3add9e5aa8d0c7114df6987.jpg[/img]


For now, the NPCs you'll be able to meet are the ones key to the story (about [b]20[/b] right now). We’re now working on adding [b]crowds[/b] ([i]communities[/i], in gamedev terminology) and runtime [b]animations [/b]to make the world feel more alive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/9c9d43bd136222482940af52df638f3b2d4b9c7e.png[/img]


[b]– animals[/b]

We’ve added [b]more animals[/b]! Now there are [b]cows[/b], [b]goats[/b], [b]wild hares[/b], [b]foxes[/b], and [b]rabbits [/b]along with the chickens. These animals will become part of the game’s flow, and [b]we need your feedback[/b] on how they feel in the game. They weren't available at the time of the last playtest, so we’ll be super grateful for any feedback on those.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/2ad517432827e92094d0d685ad4f12b8fceccb33.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/33888daf796719b3d2191d6e761e07c69bc701f4.jpg[/img]


[h2]Other changes:[/h2]

[b]– expanded narrative[/b]

We’ve designed and implemented more than [b]35 quests[/b] that take [b]about 8 hours[/b] to complete [i](if you know what you’re doing, that is)[/i]. This is just for the early part of the game – there’s still more story to come!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/9f24c3000789996acda66c5a6b25e9284819f57d.jpg[/img]


We wouldn’t want you to devour everything in one bite, though, so for the purposes of this playtest, the narrative will be [b]cut off[/b] at a certain point. Don’t worry though, you’ll still have plenty to do!


[b]– map and exploration[/b]

All locations are [b]closely tied to the story[/b] – they're not just pretty sights! We’ve [b]added new areas[/b] and[b] improved old ones[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e44d87280cd7dec39ecdb6a70419b76aa1b257f2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/1a717ab264d8332733c4eb785a36e96766be781b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/53762076683b30e5e3c7c9fe7a1c3ecc3a0ef939.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5e23283b3fee671279f6656d333f56e6c806559a.png[/img]


And we’ve got [b]a special treat[/b]! [b]Bravestand[/b], the main town in our story, which was not available for exploration at the time of the last playtest, will be all yours to experience this time! Discover all the content within all its stores, vendors, the Saloon, Town Hall, and much more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f6b29d28572b8cb4ce78f99d9d1dccab229e02dc.jpg[/img]


[b]– clothes[/b]

You can now buy or craft clothes, or just run around in your underwear! Right now, clothes are mostly for looks, but we’ll soon make them [b]affect gameplay[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/30dbaaa1066703153a3af2619e967f0b0a1d79c4.jpg[/img]



[h2]Progress from older devlogs:[/h2]

[b]– the prologue[/b]

We’ve improved the cattle drive quest – it’s smoother now! There are also [b]new dialogue options[/b] and a better tutorial, and [b]new mechanics[/b] thanks to our addition of animals into this version.


[b]– tutorials[/b]

We made the tutorials [b]simpler[/b], only showing tips when necessary. No more [b]pop-up overload[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ec58bcac8a6415326b9924552d02c08de101a24f.jpg[/img]


[b]– construction[/b]

We improved building by adding [b]object snapping[/b] and [b]shadows[/b] to show placement. It’s now easier to build and decorate with fewer restrictions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5b0ee20f67b6e2956b85e8c94d1b7fdfc43e0ecd.png[/img]


Something that we’ve currently got in the works now is the mechanic of [b]rotating objects that are already snapped to the wall[/b] – we’ll keep you updated on that in the devlogs to come.


[b]– new items[/b]

The expanded map has more things to find – items, collectibles, forage, and[b] treasure chests [/b]galore! The map is anything but empty, and so many of the newly introduced forage items will be of use in the new crafting options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/92f0b00bf6985e42d894cebdad3fe4ebfb7ce839.jpg[/img]


Plus, you’ll be getting many[b] requests[/b] from neighbors asking for items, and they’ll reward you with [b]new quests[/b] or [b]cool rewards[/b]! They will be sending you mail through your [b]mailbox[/b], so make sure to peep in there often!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f7ccf6e1390e9ac77cc145332a3c65d7b8326f1c.jpg[/img]


[b]– combat[/b]

Human enemy combat, well… it certainly is [i]there[/i]… Just kidding, we know how much everyone was asking for some cowboy shootin’, and we listened. For now, the mechanic itself is quite clunky as a whole, but it’s the one of the areas of “Cowboy’s” development we’re the [b]most focused[/b] on now.


[b]– localization[/b]

Because we’re planning for “Cowboy” to ultimately be available in many [b]different language versions[/b], we’ve added some localization options. For now much of it sounds quite funny because it’s now done with AI, but we’ll be grateful for any help with catching those language mistakes if you encounter them while playing in other language versions than English.


That's all for now. Thanks for your support, and we can’t wait to hear what you think during the next playtest!



[h2][b]!![/b][/h2]
Remember to hit that [b]“Request Access”[/b] button! We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]]. During the playtest, this will be your [b]opportunity to communicate with us[/b], [b]the devs[/b], [b]directly[/b]! We can't wait to hear from you.



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit.

notes.title: DEVLOG #12 – CREATIVE DECORATION
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/fe0e04590a7bc4f356f521ca94d82eecf7ec0f17.jpg[/img]

Thank you so much for appreciating these devlogs! The likes and engagement we’ve been seeing is super motivating! So, let’s dive into today’s topic – [b]creative decoration[/b].

Our decoration mechanic has been [b]a long time favorite[/b] among players (and ourselves too!). The description of “decoration” might be a bit misleading, though. It’s not only about placing books on shelves and the carpet at just the right angle. Most importantly, it’s about picking up and setting down [b]ANY ITEM IN THE GAME[/b], however strikes your fancy and suits your needs.

In a 3D game like “Cowboy”, not only can you make your farm look nice. You can forget crates and storages completely and just put your stuff around your home!

Before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s take a closer look at what you can accomplish using our system.



[h3]First, moving items.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/3d5db1ee016598bb6553301072354fb1843a051c.gif[/img]


[h3]Rotating objects horizontally.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/7bcd7aa4f0568258c07411cabc0a0c3d1d0bc36f.gif[/img]


[h3]Rotating objects vertically.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/18e27087c29d85eb8670055258db368ea82c5251.gif[/img]


[h3]Storage and decoration mechanic interaction.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e15b4fc7ee515e721f96b39f8bf5f4ca06f27582.gif[/img]



[h3]A little fun never hurt anybody...[/h3]

You can go for some [b]unconventional home decoration[/b], and [b]slightly chaotic level arrangements[/b]. Who wouldn’t want to climb a pyramid of pumpkins, or build a makeshift staircase using planks?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/34abc9bf09dae331409a1ec5d9400eaa8081377c.gif[/img]


[h3]Wanna see something cursed?[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/566333dc9de015e5d5ef8ac3495aa2795233026b.gif[/img]


[h3]The reasons[/h3]

So what’s the purpose of all this? Two words: [b]player freedom[/b]. We wanted to give you all a way to [b]express yourselves[/b] as freely as possible. We are very excited to see what you all come up with – chances are, a great portion of those solutions [b]we haven’t even thought of[/b] in our wildest dreams. And that is what it’s all about! Freedom of expression and creativity!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5691d1f867e4924821d66cb2ffed9b6193ead7b9.gif[/img]


[h3]Our plans for this system[/h3]

Something that is definitely within our reach and would not cause so many headaches is the system in which a player would get some decorations as a complimentary gift of sorts when they build a building. Those objects [b]would also be interactable[/b] the same way decorations and furniture is. Imagine building a workshop – wouldn’t it be cool to, once it’s built, [b]also rearrange[/b] the position of the [b]benches [/b]and [b]tables [/b]inside it?


[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]]!

notes.title: DEVLOG #11 – LIVING WORLD – IMMERSION
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners! [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/c25814c80f4914467f973a25507a16165a3f5076.png[/img]



[b]It’s Odd Qubit here[/b], and, as you might have noticed by the increase in these devlogs – we’ve really been loving this format to communicate with you all, and talk to you about the highlights of our work on “Cowboy Life Simulator”. Let’s roll in another one, this time about our [b]open and living world[/b], and [b]the immersion they bring[/b]!


[h3]NPCs[/h3]

We’ve touched a bit on our NPC system in our last devlog ([i]check it out at[/i] [i][[/i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1151380/view/4196872969306050924?l=english]this [i]link[/i][/url][i]][/i] [i]if you haven’t already![/i]), but we'll expand on it more in this one. All of our NPCs, [b]both main and secondary[/b], have their own [i]calendar [/i]– a table detailing their [i]whats[/i], [i]wheres[/i], and [i]whens[/i]. They [b]perform various chores[/b] and [b]daily activities[/b] in their designated spots, and roam freely between places they’ve need to be.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/a889e3de1b35e0becfa3696d39bf7e4ec4ef15ea.gif[/img]



NPCs can of course break out of their habits [b]to take part in a quest[/b] of your choosing, or just [b]meet with you to chat[/b]. This comes with [b]widgets and map markers[/b], reminding you which one of your neighbors has business to discuss with you.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/4c897110aea1a9c2a7ec01f3a86b3c453c985d31.png[/img]



Many NPCs also have [b]location-specific dialogue options[/b]. The Tailor will for sure want to go over his newest clothing items while at his store, but when out and about will rather talk about the weather, or the latest town gossip. Their [b]mood and attitude[/b] also change depending on what’s currently going on around town, and your actions. And once you’re done chattin’, watch out – there’s horsemen galloping through the map on their steeds at full speed!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/002c89a78a0d5f90525469abdec696d9151099a8.gif[/img]



[h3]Narrative[/h3]

The progression of the plot [b]influences the world around you[/b] as well – not only metaphorically! To give you a peek behind the narrative curtain, the first big storyline and questline you’ll encounter in the game has a lot to do with [b]a mysterious event leading to a drought[/b].

The river has suddenly run dry – it appears something or [i]someone[/i] has seen to it. If blowing up rubble dams is somehow up your alley, [b]you’re in for a treat[/b]! This will alter not only the general vista, but the very lives of the characters too, including you. That means new places to fetch water, to fish, and even just to behold sights.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/217f241e7abf27814d8bc4f46a167320bc0350e4.gif[/img]



[h3]Environment[/h3]

A life sim would not be complete without[b] a dynamic environment[/b] – a [b]night-and-day cycle[/b], as well as [b]weather [/b]and [b]fog[/b]. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/85b764e7bef8ca187868b7718608d1378b9bfa58.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f8411276c7fdac782b4ce531f1047af2be7043a0.gif[/img]



Farm animals like cattle now have [b]their own behavior styles[/b], and [b]can be interacted with[/b]. Without proper fences around their pastures, [b]cattle can run into crops[/b] and trample all over days’ worth of your hard work! As an anecdote – even one of the QA Analysts at our Pubisher’s was actually quite startled to see [b]their produce going missing[/b] as a result of forgetting to set up these fences! He was wondering where all the corn he planted had gone – it then turned out that three little chickens ate it all. We have it balanced a little more now, worry not.


And yes, Cowboy is cozy, [b]but with a little thrill[/b] – stray too far out of your farm’s bounds and you’re sure to [b]run into a wild animal or two[/b]. Or a whole wolf pack! You’d best make sure to keep those in good condition if you don’t want your Bessie or Lucy to become their next shared dinner.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/99335733d1975584e679477674d003e9d9600ff4.gif[/img]



It’s not like they’re just mindless killing machines, though. They too [b]have their own routines[/b], [b]gathering around water sources[/b] to drink, or [b]hunting for food[/b] at different points of the day – at nighttime when it comes to wolves, of course. Going to the woods to forage is not all sunshine and rainbows either, because even during the day the [b]wild boars can jump out right at ya[/b] from the tall bushes.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/c314980b1a91e26736e21ccc8fb34345fe366cf6.gif[/img]



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]]!

notes.title: DEVLOG #10 – PLAYTESTS AND FEEDBACK
notes.notes:
[h2]Howdy, partners! [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e3e99d59b8dddebb7954b1a10eea0868a80b12dc.png[/img]


[b]It’s Odd Qubit once more[/b], here to talk to you about another topic near and dear to our hearts – [b]feedback[/b]!

This spring has been a time of some increase in the community sphere for us, full of attending industry events, conferences, and kick-starting our brand new Discord server. These led to [b]connecting with players on a more hands-on level[/b], allowing us to receive fresh, new feedback.

As game developers, the feedback we receive is usually either exchanged between ourselves here at the studio, or with fellow devs. And while this type of critique offers an in-depth view provided by specialists in the field, it’s not always impartial – it’s the players’ opinions that will be the final verdict after all. As such, bringing “Cowboy Life Simulator” to them directly at indie zones at conferences or through playtests is the ultimate test – and the ultimate chance to receive their [b]raw[/b], [b]honest opinions[/b] head-on.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/848a879ea965d275f86bb6a68a82ea9b7d9397fa.png[/img]



We then carefully analyze all these observations, which often leads to new features being added, and old ones being iterated upon.

[h3]Here’s what we've already implemented![/h3]

- [b]We transformed the flow of the prologue[/b]!
It's a cowboy game, so we amped up the cowboy atmosphere, and made the whole intro much less overwhelming, and more fun! A cattle drive as your first objective? Coming up!


- [b]We revamped to the tutorial system[/b].
We reduced the amount of widgets popping up on the HUD, making the game way more approachable.


- [b]We introduced key decoration input changes[/b].
Many players found grabbing items and placing them back to be confusing. P[i]ick it up with RMB, place it back down with LMB while still holding RMB…[/i] Enough is enough! Now it’s all done with just RMB – fixed!


- [b]We brought some mechanics tweaks[/b].
The absolute top 1 suggestion by the playtesters – to put it mildly, consuming water from sources of questionable quality now inflicts undesirable intestinal issues.


- [b]More stuff to pick up[/b]!
Let’s be real here, Cowboy Life Simulator is a game about picking up stuff. And players complained there’s not much to pick up. So we’re adding more: stones, flowers, branches, herbs and the likes!




That’s not all, though.
[h3]There’s much more currently in the works![/h3]


- [b]Adding a[/b] “[b]new game[/b]” [b]option[/b]
The single-save slot is no more – start a new game whenever you wish, and load saves from previous slots. 


- [b]The ability to change the player character’s clothes[/b]
Personalization is at the heart of “Cowboy” – we’re now bringing it to the player character as well! Drop by the tailor’s store over in Bravestand and get the best cowboy looks money can buy.


- [b]More NPCs and more life on the level[/b]
The more the merrier! Observe your neighbors’ daily and weekly habits, unique to their social standing, profession, and even mood and personality. Not only that – there’s now hares, birds, butterflies… More life all around!			


- [b]Expanded narrative with more quests[/b]
Get out of the ranch for a cowboy adventure! Delve deep into what this strange land has to offer by exploring all the newly added quest-specific locations all throughout the map.


- [b]More tweaks to the decoration mechanics[/b]
Simply placing a carpet under furniture was troublesome to say the least. No more of that! It’s now much easier to maneuver, and place it under other stuff, but also upright on a wall ([i]Wild West this, cowboys that, but hey, we’re Slavs[/i]).

The furniture floating around as you’re holding it will now also cast a shadow on the ground,
so that there’s no mistake as to where it will actually land once you release that RMB.

We also have plans to make the furniture being held snap to the walls – that’s much easier
said than done though. But we do love a challenge!



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message at our Instagram – @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our growing Discord server – here’s the link! [https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]


Happy trails, friend.

notes.title: Getting cowboys into the world...
notes.notes:
I dare say that in many places our game looks better than some productions of a company making AAAA games. A bold statement, but justified. While traversing our world, I often find myself stopping for a moment to admire what I have on the screen.

However, let's recall how our world looked a little over a year ago.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/bc506bf525834ad6a02b67b8d155445f2fc0b45d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/3fc91041f78c9d8ef851e60b4729844481ab9237.png[/img]

We were not satisfied with that. We decided to make the whole game world from scratch. We asked ourselves at the beginning: what should our world look like?
We all unanimously answered that it should be nice and cowboyish.

However, nothing is as simple as one would like. We do not have a lot of resources that would allow us to put a large amount of detail in each location. For this reason, we decided to focus on landscapes. We try to keep our levels clean, not cluttering them with unnecessary detail where it could distract the player's eye from a nice view. This is facilitated by the light styling of our graphics.
When working on a level, we constantly think about the fact that there has to be "something" in a place and it has to be about "something." We collect a variety of images for inspiration and turn the coolest ones into something you'll see in our game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f96a4ac6710f489bb18773ce6cf8b3f88fff2e45.png[/img]

In the end, what did we come up with?
So we decided to divide our map into 3 main regions, which you can see below.

[h2]Step [/h2]
This is the area we spent the most time on and went through the most iterations. This is where the player will spend the most time, because this is where they will build their farm.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/4b4d8528fe3f467c6cc61c710413a8634cde3e02.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e793411e7ef73c1a8e717bcb56539753561d2e17.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/2b5ac48d557335c9a977359ff92b93f889dd2f67.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ba32bac0b77ac35a2e95087592f085219507814a.png[/img]

[h2]Trappers' grounds[/h2]
Here we built a factory where trappers trade in various goods. It is mainly mountains and forests.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5b2b0608357cfcda510da8e1378b64f61d932fba.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f292578cf2f154a092539b5c0a79dbdef2dc7bfc.png[/img]

[h2]Desert[/h2]
The player gains access to this area only in the third act of the game. Somewhere here there is a mine that is very worth visiting.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/64a77e65508000185544e6f61db62e922daa0012.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/d91d9840fbf4b0f4d335adbf714ab3b551dec997.png[/img]

Something we are particularly proud of is how the look of our game changes from hour to hour. Every morning and evening, it's a moment where I stop and wonder why I'm just sitting in front of a computer making games, instead of being a cowboy and being able to look at such things live.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/8efa6c10be3f55a3f6e206c8da2d23c26f6a5232.gif[/img]

But what does it look like from the level designer's side?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e3a8a29f2c60b1af63ec4bbe2a3cf1f8057f2c11.png[/img]
It just looks like CHAOS. With the red poles, we mark for ourselves things that look bad or something needs to be improved. The blue ones are pastures, and the green ones are some other important locations.

And in the screenshot below you can see something you can't see in the game. Various types of triggers, splines and such.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/0588a1b0c8fea830362d3bbc32a2e7c56f546c59.gif[/img]

There are also some interesting slip-ups. The following screen shot was taken by our art director after someone added fish swimming in a pond. Something was messed up with the scale.
